insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited

great.name: NCB
great.quote: a sum equal to 10% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring Policy shall be provided as Cumulative Bonus irrespective of any claims
great.reference: Section B, III. Renewal Benefits, 2. Cumulative Bonus (Page 16)
great.explanation: A 10% Cumulative Bonus is added on renewal irrespective of any claims. Your bonus does not reduce or reset to zero after a claim, which is better than most NCB designs.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: Instant addition of 100% Basic Sum Insured on complete or partial utilization of Your existing Policy Sum Insured and cumulative Bonus (if applicable) during the Policy Year... The Sum Insured will be restored only once in a Policy Year.
good.reference: Section B, II. Other Benefits, 1. Restore benefit (Page 11)
good.explanation: Adds 100% of Basic Sum Insured after complete or partial use of your Sum Insured (and cumulative bonus, if applicable), but only once in a policy year. This can help pay a second hospitalization in the same year, but the refill is limited to a single restore.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.reference: Section C, 1(ii) Pre-Existing Diseases: Code - Excl01 (Page 19)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with us.
good.reference: Section C, 1(i) Specified disease/procedure waiting period: Code - Excl02 (Page 16-18)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage. This is in line with common market practice.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-Hospitalization Medical expenses... incurred upto 30 days before Hospitalisation.
good.reference: Section B, I.2 Pre-Hospitalization Medical expenses (Page 10)
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses incurred up to 30 days before hospitalization. This helps reimburse diagnostics and consultations leading up to admission.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Non-Medical expenses such as... Full list of Non-Medical expenses is attached... Annexure I - List of Non-Medical Expenses... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 68 VASOFIX SAFETY ...
bad.reference: Section C, 3. Specific Exclusions (Page 22) + Annexure I (Pages 41-42)
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items (e.g., gloves, masks, cannula/vasofix items) are excluded as per the annexure list. You will likely pay these hospital bill components out of pocket even in a cashless claim.

bad.name: Co-pay (Optional)
bad.quote: If opted and mentioned on the Policy Schedule that a Co-payment is effective... the insured person shall bear 20% of the eligible claim amount payable under the Policy
bad.reference: Section D, 2. Specific General Terms, Clause 15. Co-Payment (Page 34)
bad.explanation: If co-payment is opted and shown on the Policy Schedule, you must bear 20% of each eligible claim amount. This directly increases your out-of-pocket cost on every claim where it applies.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: In-Patient Treatment... includes: • Hospital room rent or boarding
unclear.explanation: Hospital room rent/boarding is covered as part of in-patient treatment, but no room category or rupee cap is stated here. Any room-rent restriction (and possible linked deductions) would typically be confirmed in the Policy Schedule.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
